papers.title: Sea-fishing cultures show rare blend of tight social ties and openness to strangers.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: Research has linked cultural differences to historical subsistence styles, but most studies have focused on farming or herding. Sea fishing is a major subsistence style, yet we know much less about whether fishing shapes culture. We propose an explanation for why fishing has received less attention-its cultural patterns do not fit neatly into the individualism-collectivism dichotomy that has been so useful in studies of farming and herding. First, we tested 1,010 people from nearby regions in Japan as a more controlled comparison. Then we tested the generalizability of the findings across 150 contemporary nations and historical records from 1,265 ethnic groups worldwide. People from fishing regions think holistically and emphasize responsibilities in close relationships more than people in nonfishing cultures (culture level d = 0.91). These characteristics are more common in collectivistic cultures and may have been adaptive for cooperation in dangerous seas. However, they show less ingroup loyalty and less outgroup discrimination (d = 1.37), which is more similar to individualistic cultures. Openness to outsiders may have been adaptive for fishing's mobility and flexible labor networks. We address reverse causality by running instrumental variable analyses using data on environmental suitability for fishing. To pinpoint fishing, we compare regions that have coastlines, some by seas that support large fish populations and others that support few fish. Results show access to the ocean, trade, or transportation are not linked to these cultural differences. Finally, the cultural patterns do not extend to freshwater fishing, which has different demands from sea fishing.

papers.title: Gambling Harms: Locating the harm from gambling alongside substance addiction using Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis.
papers.abstract: Introduction Gambling harm has previously been treated differently from substance addiction in policy and regulation, despite emerging evidence of comparable population-level harm. However, direct comparison between gambling - a behavioural addiction - and substance addictions is difficult. Current understandings of harm can rely heavily on physical functioning and do not reflect the holistic harms associated with gambling. We aim to (1) compare harms from gambling alongside substances; (2) characterise the contribution of different harm components; and (3) assess the robustness of these rankings. Methods Using Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA), we systematically compared gambling harms at three risk levels (low, medium, and high) with high-risk use of alcohol, cocaine, and cannabis. A purposively sampled expert panel comprising lived experience, research, treatment, and policy/advocacy perspectives was convened, each member having backgrounds in at least two of the harms assessed. The panel assessed harm to self and others across seven components: mental wellbeing, physical wellbeing, finances, ethical lapses, work/study and meaningful activities, close relationships, and social relationships. Results The model ranked high-risk gambling (harm score 0-100: 94.8) and high-risk alcohol (94.7) as essentially equally harmful, followed by high-risk cocaine (86.9). While substance addictions produced greater physical wellbeing harm in the model, gambling caused disproportionate financial harm and comparable relationship harm. Notably, harm to others equalled harm to self across all options. Rankings remained stable across plausible parameter variations in sensitivity testing. Conclusion These findings converge with independent evidence from health utility studies and holistic harm frameworks, demonstrating that high-risk gambling produces comparable harm to high-risk alcohol when assessed through a public health lens rather than purely physiological criteria. papers.title: First report of the emergence of duck hepatitis virus 1 associated with duck viral hepatitis in young ducklings in Bangladesh.
papers.abstract: Duck hepatitis virus (DHV) is the etiological agent of duck viral hepatitis (DVH), a highly contagious disease associated with significant mortality in ducklings. This study aimed to detect and molecularly characterize DHV in young ducklings from the Netrokona and Kishoreganj districts of Bangladesh between February and May 2025. Thirty-five liver tissue samples were collected from ducklings suspected of DVH based on clinical history, observed symptoms, and post-mortem lesions. Samples underwent histopathological examination and RNA extraction, followed by reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). For further confirmation, partial sequencing of the 5'-UTR of a DHV-1-positive isolate was performed, and evolutionary relationships were evaluated through phylogenetic analysis and BLAST search using the NCBI GenBank database. Clinically, affected ducklings exhibited angular arch posture, with mortality rates ranging from 35% to 80% among 4- to 10-day-old birds. Post-mortem examination revealed enlarged, yellowish-brown livers with ecchymotic or pinpoint hemorrhages. Histopathology demonstrated hepatocellular necrosis, hemorrhage, and congestion of the central and portal veins and sinusoids, accompanied by severe inflammatory infiltration. RT-PCR identified DHV-1 in 8 (23%) samples. Phylogenetic and BLAST analyses demonstrated a close relationship (97.26%-98.28% identity) between Bangladeshi isolates and DHV-1 isolates from India, China, and Taiwan. To our knowledge, this is the first study in Bangladesh to confirm DHV-1 infection as the cause of DVH in young ducklings, emphasizing the urgent need for vaccination to prevent DHV-1-related mortality.IMPORTANCEOutbreaks of duck viral hepatitis (DVH) have been reported around the globe. In Bangladesh, although duck farmers and veterinarians often complained of deaths in ducklings showing symptoms consistent with DVH, no documented studies have previously confirmed Duck hepatitis virus (DHV) infection. papers.title: Lived Experiences of Patients With Permanent Colostomy in Wolaita Sodo Town, South Ethiopia: A Descriptive Phenomenological Qualitative Study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Permanent colostomy affects the physical, psychological, spiritual, and social well-being of the patients. However, little is known about the lived experiences of patients with permanent colostomy in the study area. Therefore, the aim of this study was to explore the lived experience of permanent colostomy patients in Wolaita Sodo town, south Ethiopia. METHODS: A purposeful sampling technique was used in this study with 12 adult volunteers with permanent colostomies. Data were analyzed using Colaizzi's descriptive phenomenological study design, with OpenCode Version 4.02 software used for the analysis. RESULTS: Five main themes emerged from the analysis: emotional and psychological experience, altered embodiment and intimate relationships, changed social life, coping and adaptation, and healthcare support. Each main theme included related subthemes. CONCLUSION: The permanent colostomy significantly changed participants' daily routines, affecting every part of their lives, including their personal and social relationships. Participants described understanding, acceptance, and close communication as important elements for long-term adaptation.

papers.title: Early Adolescent Romantic Experiences and Psychosocial Stress in Sexual Minority and Heterosexual Youth.
papers.abstract: Sexual minority youth are at greater risk for negative psychosocial outcomes starting in early adolescence. We examined early romantic involvement as a risk or protective factor for sexual minority youth compared to heterosexual youth. This study examined associations among youth romantic experiences, sexual orientation, and psychosocial stress from early (age 12) to middle (age 15) adolescence (N = 392; n = 348 heterosexual youth, n = 44 sexual minority youth). Although heterosexual and sexual minority youth had similar levels of early romantic experiences, early adolescent romantic experiences were uniquely associated with poorer concurrent and subsequent psychiatric symptoms and psychosocial outcomes among sexual minority youth; however, romantic experience in middle adolescence was not associated with concurrent increased psychological stress for sexual minority youth. Early adolescent, but not middle adolescent, romantic experiences are associated with heightened negative psychosocial outcomes among sexual minority youth. Timing of romantic involvement may determine whether romantic experiences are a risk or protective factor for this population.

papers.title: Phylogenomic analyses shed new light on the phylogeny and historical biogeography of the water lily genus Nymphaea (Nymphaeaceae).
papers.abstract: Nymphaea is the most species-rich, geographically widespread, and phenotypically diverse genus in the basal angiosperm order Nymphaeales. Species of this genus possess considerable ornamental, cultural, medicinal, and ecological value. However, phylogenetic relationships among species and the biogeographic history of this genus remain incompletely understood. Here, we conducted a comprehensive phylogenomic study of Nymphaea using cytoplasmic (plastid and mitochondrial) and nuclear genomic sequence data. Our phylogenetic analyses supported the merger of the genera Victoria and Euryale into Nymphaea. The significant phylogenetic discordance detected within Nymphaea was attributed to both incomplete lineage sorting and reticulate evolution. Moreover, network analyses suggested that hybridization and "ghost introgression" have likely been widespread throughout the evolutionary history of the genus. Molecular dating and biogeographic analyses indicated that Nymphaea originated in the Oriental region during the mid-Cretaceous and subsequently dispersed to other regions, where multiple centers of diversification were established. Long-distance dispersal and vicariance appear to have jointly shaped the intercontinental distribution of the genus. These findings provide new insights into the phylogeny and evolutionary history of Nymphaea.

papers.title: Taxonomy, developmental biology, and host interaction of Kriechbaumerella dendrolimi (Hymenoptera: Chalcididae), a pupal parasitoid wasp parasitizing the Chinese oak silkworm.
papers.abstract: The Chinese oak silkworm (COS), Antheraea pernyi (Guérin-Méneville) (Lepidoptera: Saturniidae), is economically important in sericulture and related applications. In this study, a pupal parasitoid associated with COS in Guizhou, China, was identified as Kriechbaumerella dendrolimi Sheng & Zhong primarily on the basis of morphological characters, with mitochondrial COI and nuclear 28S rDNA sequences provided as supplementary molecular reference data. Detailed observations of adult morphology, reproductive structures, immature stages, and courtship and mating behavior are presented. We also compared the performance of K. dendrolimi on COS pupae originating from Guizhou and Jilin. Adult offspring per host pupa among hosts with successful parasitoid emergence was significantly higher in Jilin-origin hosts than in Guizhou-origin hosts, whereas parasitism rate, adult emergence rate, female proportion, and developmental duration did not differ significantly between the two host populations. Cocoon-pupa spacing was significantly greater in Jilin-origin than in Guizhou-origin hosts. Ovipositor length numerically overlapped the range of cocoon-pupa spacing observed in both populations; however, these measurements were not paired at the individual level, and no functional relationship between the two traits was inferred. These findings provide taxonomic and biological baseline information for future studies of K. dendrolimi-COS interactions and host-related variation in parasitoid performance.

papers.title: Dynamic Commercial Silicones Toward Sustainable, Task-Reconfigurable Suction Gripping.
papers.abstract: Silicone suction cups are widely used in industrial automation for scalable, high-throughput handling, yet conventional designs are restricted to limited geometries. Advancing toward gripping is essential to transition robotics from single-task execution to versatile handling across dynamic environments but presents a fundamental materials challenge: balancing the properties of on-demand geometric reconfigurability with operational strength and elasticity. Existing universal grippers typically utilize composite materials that couple shape adaptation and gripping operation within a single cycle, introducing critical performance trade-offs in force, speed, and preload requirements while adding structural complexity that together hinder broad industrial adoption. To address this, we establish a versatile post-fabrication strategy that transforms commercial silicone thermosets into dynamic silicone materials via catalyst-mediated exchange of intrinsic siloxane bonds. This enables scalable transformation of industrial suction cups to reconfigurable grippers that reconfigure shapes at elevated temperatures while preserving high gripping performance via thermosetting properties at ambient temperatures. We demonstrate an all-silicone, hierarchically structured suction gripper combining a reconfigurable load-bearing body with a compliant sealing interface towards sustainable, task-reconfigurable gripping, ensuring infrastructure compatibility while delivering rapid suction actuation (50 ms) following thermal reconfiguration (e.g., ∼30 min at 140°C), efficient load capacity (27 kPa), and zero-preload attachment across diverse environments.

papers.title: Multi-Scale Structural Degradation Mechanisms in Ni-Rich NCM Cathodes.
papers.abstract: Ni-rich layered oxides (LiNixCoyMnzO2, x > 0.8, NCM) are among the most promising cathode materials for high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries, yet increasing nickel content intrinsically amplifies structural instability during deep delithiation and prolonged cycling. The resulting performance decay is not governed by an individual failure mode, but emerges from coupled evolution of electronic/chemical-bonding, local atomic, lattice/phase, and particle/interface levels. This review establishes a multiscale structure-performance framework. The evolution of Ni 3d-O 2p hybridization and oxygen redox activity modifies metal-oxygen bonding, triggering local structural disorder, lattice reconstruction, and strain accumulation. These changes promote particle cracking and interfacial degradation, while particle damage further accelerates electrolyte reactions and oxygen loss through feedback interactions, establishing a self-amplifying degradation network. By integrating operando characterization and theoretical analysis, this review identifies critical coupling nodes and provides mechanism-guided principles for rational modification strategies. Future efforts should develop predictive multiscale design frameworks that bridge fundamental degradation mechanisms with practical engineering of next-generation Ni-rich cathodes.

papers.title: Flexible nitrogen- and oxygen-rich triazine covalent organic frameworks for the efficient extraction and detection of estrogens in river water and human urine.
papers.abstract: As endocrine disruptors, estrogens pose serious risks to the human health and ecological environments. Therefore, sensitive and reliable analysis of estrogens in complex samples remains essential yet challenging. Herein, a flexible nitrogen- and oxygen-rich triazine covalent organic framework (COF; referred to as COF), was prepared using 2,4,6-tris(4-aminophenoxy)-1,3,5-triazine and 2,4,6- tris(4-formylphenoxy)-1,3,5-triazine (TPT--CHO) as monomers. For comparison, semiflexible COF-2 and COF-3 were synthesized by replacing TPT-CHO with 4,4',4″-(1,3,5-triazine-2,4,6-triyl)tribenzaldehyde (Ttb) and 1,3,5-tris(p- formylphenyl)benzene (Tfb) as ligands, respectively. Furthermore, rigid COF-4 and COF-5 were synthesized via the reaction of 2,4,6-tri(4-aminophenyl)-1,3,5-triazine with Ttb and Tfb, respectively. In addition, rigid COF-6 was synthesized by reacting 1,3,5-tri(4-aminophenyl)benzene with Tfb. These COFs, which exhibited varying nitrogen and oxygen aton densities, were used as adsorbents for estriol (E3). Owing to its flexible structure and the highest nitrogen and oxygen atom densities among the COFs, COF-1 showed the highest E3 adsorption capacity. Density functional theory calculations and various characterization techniques demonstrated that estrogen adsorption on COF-1 mainly relied on pore-size matching and hydrogen-bonding, π-π, electrostatic, and hydrophobic interactions. Moreover, COF-1-based dispersive solid-phase extraction coupled with high-performance liquid chromatography-ultraviolet spectroscopy exhibited an excellent linearity range (estradiol and E3: 1-100 ng/mL; diethylstilbestrol: 0.5-100 ng/mL), low limits of detection (0.12-0.25 ng/mL), and excellent recoveries (75.20%-110.92%) in river water and human urine samples.

papers.title: Living Together, Loving Apart: Health, Sexuality and Relationships in Middle-Aged and Older Men in Europe.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Over time, family structures have grown more complex, diversifying adult relationships. While research has compared marital, cohabiting and living apart together relationships based on quality and health, less is known about their sexual dynamics. Theoretical frameworks suggest that co-resident relationships may integrate sexuality differently from living apart together unions, where physical separation can either strengthen or weaken sexual intimacy. This study addresses this gap by analysing sexual function and satisfaction among men in marital, cohabiting and living apart together relationships. Exploring the relationship between living apart together unions and sexual and hormonal aspects can enhance our understanding of the links between hormones and the social and relational dynamics of contemporary society. METHODS: We analysed cross-sectional data from the European Male Ageing Study, a non-interventional cohort study conducted in eight European countries from 2005 to 2008. The sample included 3259 men aged 40-79 years who reported their relationship status. Sexual function was evaluated using the validated European Male Ageing Study sexual function questionnaire. Hormonal, lifestyle and health indicators were also collected. Statistical analyses, including ANCOVA, were used to adjust for confounders such as age, education, lifestyle and comorbidities. RESULTS: Living apart together relationships were reported by 6.9% of the cohort, similar to the 7.0% in cohabiting relationships, while 86.0% were married. Living apart together men were younger, more educated, and had a higher prevalence of smoking compared to married men. Compared to those in co-residential relationships, men in living apart together relationships showed higher levels of free testosterone, greater sexual desire and satisfaction, and increased frequency of sexual activity, morning erections and masturbation. papers.title: Community environment has similar risks for subsequent maltreatment reports as risk factors: The impact of structural disadvantage on child protective service involvement.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Child maltreatment rates remain stable despite prevention efforts, suggesting the need to reevaluate prevailing assumptions about the causes of maltreatment and broaden the focus beyond individual or family level characteristics to include structural and contextual factors. OBJECTIVE: This study evaluates whether neighborhood disadvantage predicts recurrent child protective services (CPS) involvement following an initial accepted report. PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: The sample included 45,378 families with an accepted CPS report and no prior history from a public child welfare agency between 2014 and 2018. Families were followed for 12 months, and addresses were geocoded to census tract level. METHODS: Family-level administrative data were matched to the Area Deprivation Index (ADI). Multinomial logistic regression estimated associations between ADI and report status (no report, subsequent report (SR) and substantiated subsequent report (SSR)), adjusting for victim age, child abuse/neglect indicators, intimate partner violence, mental health/substance use, maltreatment type, family composition, Gini coefficient, limited English, and race/ethnicity. Predicted probabilities were examined across ADI levels and covariate profiles. RESULTS: The community environment was a significant predictor of the odds of an SR and SSR. Within ADI levels, SR rates were often similar for families with and without specific risk factors, whereas SSR rates were consistently higher for families with those risk factors. Race/ethnicity differences within ADI levels were small. CONCLUSIONS: The risk from community disadvantage persists after adjusting for individually measured, micro-level, risk factors. Findings support expanding secondary prevention beyond family-focused services to include poverty reduction and material supports.
